CredFile is a path to a file whose contents are the password (the org
api_key_file posture). Resolve reads it when CredEnv is unset.
leaves.help: A path to a file whose contents are the password (the org api_key_file posture). Resolve reads it when CredEnv is unset.

leaves.doc: From is the envelope + header From address. Required when Enabled.
leaves.help: The envelope + header From address. Required when Enabled.

leaves.doc: To is the default recipient list used when a consumer supplies none.
leaves.help: The default recipient list used when a consumer supplies none.

leaves.doc: TLSMode ∈ starttls | tls | none. Empty defaults to starttls.
leaves.help: ∈ starttls | tls | none. Empty defaults to starttls.

leaves.doc: Auth ∈ "" (auto) | plain | login. Empty auto-selects.
leaves.help: ∈ "" (auto) | plain | login. Empty auto-selects.

leaves.doc:
TimeoutSeconds bounds one full send (dial + handshake + conversation).
0 defaults to 15.
leaves.help: Bounds one full send (dial + handshake + conversation). 0 defaults to 15.

leaves.doc:
Enabled gates the scheduler. Default false (opt-in; a fired digest makes
an outbound SMTP call).
leaves.help: Gates the scheduler. Default false (opt-in; a fired digest makes an outbound SMTP call).

leaves.doc: Frequency ∈ weekly | monthly. Empty defaults to weekly.
leaves.help: ∈ weekly | monthly. Empty defaults to weekly.

leaves.doc:
SendHour is the UTC hour (0-23) at/after which a due digest is sent on the
first tick of a new period. Default 8.
leaves.help: The UTC hour (0-23) at/after which a due digest is sent on the first tick of a new period. Default 8.

leaves.doc:
To overrides the recipient list for digests. Empty falls back to
[email].to (resolved by the caller before sending).
leaves.help: Overrides the recipient list for digests. Empty falls back to [email].to (resolved by the caller before sending).

leaves.doc:
Enabled gates the whole subsystem: the OTLP /v1/traces receiver,
the obs_* schema (applied only when true), ingestion, the
trajectory API, and the eval plane. Default false.
leaves.help: Turns AI Apps on: this machine receives your apps' traces and shows them on the AI Apps pages.

leaves.doc:
OnlineSampleRate, in (0,1], runs OnlineScorers over that fraction of
live LLM spans as they ingest (the Langfuse/Arize online-eval model).
0 (default) disables online sampling entirely.
leaves.help: The share of your apps' model calls scored as they arrive, from 0 (off, the default) to 1 (every call).

leaves.doc:
OnlineScorers are the scorer specs run during online sampling, each a
string "name" or "name:key=val,key2=val2". Only facts-based code
scorers make sense online (status_ok / latency_under / cost_under) —
content scorers need a stored body. Empty disables online sampling.
leaves.help: The scorers run on the sampled calls, by name. Scorers that read only the trace's facts suit live scoring best.

leaves.doc:
JudgeModel names the model an llm_judge scorer uses by default (when a
scorer spec omits its own model=). Empty disables the LLM judge: the
host JudgeClient stays unbound, llm_judge errors clearly, and code
scorers run fully offline. The judge call is the ONLY outbound network
in the subsystem and runs ONLY for an explicitly-invoked `observer eval
run` (never the daemon/online-sampling path).
leaves.help: The model an LLM judge scorer uses. Empty turns the LLM judge off.

leaves.doc:
JudgeBaseURL is the OpenAI-compatible chat-completions base URL the
judge posts to. Empty defaults to OpenRouter (https://openrouter.ai/api/v1).
leaves.help: The OpenAI-compatible address the judge calls. Empty uses OpenRouter.

leaves.doc:
JudgeAPIKeyEnv names the ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE holding the judge API key
— the key is never written to config or disk (the pi/hermes launcher
posture). Empty defaults to OPENROUTER_API_KEY.
leaves.help: The name of the environment variable that holds the judge's API key. The key itself is never stored.

leaves.doc: Model names the judge model. Empty = judge disabled.
leaves.help: The judge model. Empty turns the judge off.

leaves.doc:
BaseURL is the OpenAI-compatible chat-completions base URL. Empty
defaults to OpenRouter (https://openrouter.ai/api/v1) at the binding.
leaves.help: The OpenAI-compatible address the judge calls. Empty uses OpenRouter.

leaves.doc:
APIKeyEnv names the ENV VAR holding the judge API key — never the key
itself. Empty defaults to OPENROUTER_API_KEY. Loopback/local judges
need no key (the binding treats a loopback base_url as no-egress and
allows an empty/unset key).
leaves.help: The name of the environment variable that holds the judge's API key. The key itself is never stored. A judge on this machine needs none.

leaves.doc:
TimeoutMS bounds a single judge call. 0 = the default for where the
judge runs: 1500 ms for a loopback judge (the admission budget) and
8000 ms for a hosted one, whose first call (TLS set-up plus a reasoning
model's thinking) outlasted 1.5 s live; an org-relay judge defaults to
10000 ms.
leaves.help: Bounds a single judge call. 0 = the default for where the judge runs: 1500 ms for a loopback judge (the admission budget) and 8000 ms for a hosted one, whose first call (TLS set-up plus a reasoning model's thinking) outlasted 1.5 s live; an org-relay judge defaults to 10000 ms.

leaves.doc:
MaxTokens caps the judge REPLY length (the reply is only a short JSON
verdict). 0 = the binding's default. A tight cap bounds latency + cost
on a hosted judge and stops a chatty local model from streaming forever.
leaves.help: Caps the judge REPLY length (the reply is only a short JSON verdict). 0 = the binding's default. A tight cap bounds latency + cost on a hosted judge and stops a chatty local model from streaming forever.

leaves.doc:
NumCtx is an Ollama-style context-window hint passed through ONLY to a
loopback/local judge (a hosted OpenAI-compatible API rejects unknown
fields, so it is never sent remotely). 0 = omit. Its effect depends on
the local host honoring the field on its /v1/chat/completions endpoint.
leaves.help: An Ollama-style context-window hint passed through ONLY to a loopback/local judge (a hosted OpenAI-compatible API rejects unknown fields, so it is never sent remotely). 0 = omit. Its effect depends on the local host honoring the field on its /v1/chat/completions endpoint.

leaves.doc:
RequestProfile is how the judge request is shaped: "auto" (or empty,
the default) picks from the model id (bare OpenAI GPT-5 and o-series
ids get "reasoning", everything else "chat"); "chat" sends max_tokens
and temperature 0 (OpenAI-compatible chat models, local servers);
"reasoning" sends max_completion_tokens, no temperature and a
reasoning effort, which OpenAI's reasoning models require (they refuse
max_tokens and temperature 0). Set it for a model id auto cannot
recognise, such as an Azure deployment name.
leaves.help: How the judge request is shaped: "auto" (or empty, the default) picks from the model id; "chat" sends max_tokens and temperature 0 (OpenAI-compatible chat models, local servers); "reasoning" sends max_completion_tokens, no temperature and a reasoning effort, which OpenAI's reasoning models require (they refuse max_tokens and temperature 0). default (minimal for gpt-5 / -mini / -nano, low for later GPT-5 and the

leaves.doc: Enabled gates admission WITHIN the obs subsystem. Default false.
leaves.help: Turns admission on: requests your app sends through this machine are checked before they reach the model.

leaves.doc:
Mode is off | observe | enforce. P1 ships observe only; enforce is P2.
Empty is treated as "observe" when Enabled.
leaves.help: Off, observe (record each decision, never block) or enforce (apply it). Empty means observe while admission is on.

leaves.doc:
Strict = fail-closed on judge error/timeout (Deny). Default false =
fail-open (Allow + recorded admission_error). BACK-COMPAT ALIAS: prefer
OnJudgeError, which is the explicit posture enum. When OnJudgeError is
empty, Strict resolves the posture (strict=true → fail_closed); when
OnJudgeError is set, it wins and Strict is ignored.
leaves.help: Deny a request when the judge fails or times out. Off allows it and records the error. The judge error setting says the same more clearly and wins when set.

leaves.doc:
OnJudgeError is the explicit judge-unavailable posture:
"fail_open" (Allow, today's default) or "fail_closed" (Deny). Empty =
resolve from Strict. This is the enum form of Strict; the invasive
request-queueing posture is deliberately NOT offered here (it would need
a new proxy admit-result shape). LOCAL-ONLY, never distributed.
leaves.help: What happens when the judge cannot answer: allow the request (fail open) or deny it (fail closed).

leaves.doc:
JudgeRetries is how many EXTRA bounded in-process attempts the admission
engine makes on a judge transport error before the posture fires. 0 =
no retry (today's behavior). A cheap reliability lever for a flaky or
cold-starting judge; it does not change the synchronous verdict contract.
leaves.help: How many EXTRA bounded in-process attempts the admission engine makes on a judge transport error before the posture fires. 0 = no retry (today's behavior). A cheap reliability lever for a flaky or cold-starting judge; it does not change the synchronous verdict contract.

leaves.doc: Scope is last_user | conversation. P1 = last_user; conversation is P3.
leaves.help: What the judge reads: the last user message (the default) or the whole conversation.

leaves.doc: RetentionDays bounds the obs_admission_events audit table. 0 = keep.
leaves.help: How many days admission decisions are kept on this machine. 0 keeps them.

MaxTokens caps the judge REPLY length (the reply is only a short JSON

Patterns that let a request through without asking the judge.
Patterns that deny a request without asking the judge.
The longest message allowed, in bytes: a longer one is denied without asking the judge. 0 is no limit.

leaves.doc:
SecretRemoteJudge is the local decision (allow|flag|ask|deny) applied
when the request carries a pattern-certain secret AND the judge is
REMOTE — the request is NOT egressed to the hosted judge; the configured
decision is returned locally instead (spec §3 layer 3). Empty/"allow" =
off (the request still goes to the — already secret-scrubbed, §item 8 —
remote judge). Inert for a local/off judge.
leaves.help: The decision when a request carries a secret and the judge runs off this machine. The request is never sent to that judge.

leaves.doc: CacheTTLS is the verdict-cache TTL in seconds. 0 = the svc default.
leaves.help: The verdict-cache TTL in seconds. 0 = the svc default.

leaves.doc:
JudgeChunkBytes bounds a single judge call's content size: a request
longer than this is split into overlapping windows, each judged, and the
verdicts reduced strictest-wins (map-reduce, spec §4 — mirrors the demo's
app-layer chunking, now in-core). 0 = the engine default (3500).
leaves.help: Bounds a single judge call's content size: a request longer than this is split into overlapping windows, each judged, and the verdicts reduced strictest-wins. 0 = the engine default (3500).

leaves.doc:
JudgeChunkOverlapBytes is the overlap between adjacent judge windows so a
concern straddling a boundary is still seen whole by one chunk. 0 = the
engine default (200); clamped below JudgeChunkBytes.
leaves.help: The overlap between adjacent judge windows so a concern straddling a boundary is still seen whole by one chunk. 0 = the engine default (200); clamped below JudgeChunkBytes.

finding — default false).

the end-user identity from — the app shares it as an integration
requirement (the SDK path passes `user` directly and ignores this).

is inert for that request (the app-wide policy still applies).
leaves.help: The request header your app puts each end user's id in, so limits apply per user.

WebhookURL (an outbound network call), so alerting is explicit opt-in.
leaves.help: Turns alerts on. Off by default, because a fired alert can send data to a webhook.

leaves.doc:
WebhookURL receives the fired-alert JSON payload (one POST per crossing).
Empty = record fired events (visible via `observer obs alerts`) but send
no webhook — the node stays egress-free.
leaves.help: The address each fired alert is posted to. Empty records alerts on this machine and sends nothing.

leaves.doc:
Email, when true, ALSO delivers each fired alert as an email through the
shared [email] channel (which must itself be enabled). This is the
per-consumer opt-in mirroring WebhookURL — an ADDITIONAL delivery target,
not a replacement. Default false.
leaves.help: Also email each fired alert, through this machine's email settings (which must be on).

leaves.doc:
EmailTo overrides the [email].to default recipients for this node's alert
emails. Empty falls back to [email].to.
leaves.help: Who gets alert emails. Empty uses the recipients in this machine's email settings.

leaves.doc: EvalIntervalMinutes is how often the evaluator ticks. 0 defaults to 5.
leaves.help: How often alert rules are checked, in minutes. 0 means every 5.

leaves.doc:
SlackWebhookURL is a Slack incoming-webhook URL every fired alert is
also posted to (W3-5). A SECRET: never rendered or logged; written only
through PUT /api/obs/alerts/slack or `observer obs alerts slack set`.
Only https://hooks.slack.com/ and hooks.slack-gov.com URLs are
accepted. Empty = no Slack delivery.
leaves.help: A Slack incoming webhook each fired alert is posted to. Kept secret: never shown after it is saved.

leaves.doc:
PagerDutyRoutingKey is a PagerDuty Events API v2 routing (integration)
key (W5-5): a fire triggers an incident and the rule's clear resolves
it. A SECRET: never rendered or logged; written only through
PUT /api/obs/alerts/pagerduty or `observer obs alerts pagerduty set`.
Empty = no PagerDuty delivery.
leaves.help: A PagerDuty routing key: a fired alert opens an incident and its clear resolves it. Kept secret: never shown after it is saved.

leaves.doc:
Mode is off | advise | enforce. advise evaluates + logs the directive but
never applies it; enforce applies it on the proxy path. Empty ⇒ off.
leaves.help: Off, advise (record where a request would go, change nothing) or enforce (route it).

leaves.doc:
CooldownSeconds is the hold window for a same-session budget-band model
switch (design §3.6 / finding 11) — a cost switch is held within this
window; verdict/locality switches never hold. 0 = the boundary default.
leaves.help: How long a conversation stays on a model after a cost switch, in seconds.

leaves.owned_by: config.toml directly (a compound table the generic editor does not render)
leaves.doc: Rules is the first-match-wins rule table.
leaves.help: The routing rules, checked in order; the first match wins.

Targets is the typed upstream target table (id + url + shape). A declared
shape is REQUIRED for any enforce-mode route_to_upstream (design finding
6) — [proxy.upstreams] entries carry only URLs.
leaves.help: The model endpoints a rule can route to.

leaves.doc: Cohorts is an optional end-user → cohort map (LOCAL-ONLY).
leaves.help: Groups of end users that rules can name. Kept on this machine.

leaves.doc:
ProxyTurnTraces is the "gateway rail" (docs/observability.md "proxy
turn (automatic)"): when true (and Enabled is true), a proxied LLM
turn that arrived on an explicit /up/<id> upstream lane — the lane a
co-resident hosted app is pointed at (e.g. Open WebUI via
/up/openrouter) — is synthesized into an obs_traces/obs_spans pair
(chat.turn/chat.completions) at insert time, so it appears in the org
Trajectory explorer without the app instrumenting anything.

PLANE BOUNDARY: synthesis covers ONLY /up/<id> lane traffic. The
default provider lanes (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, codex base_url, gemini)
carry Plane-B coding agents, whose rail is api_turns → sessions → the
coding-agent org rollups; they must never appear in the Hosted Apps
(Plane A) Trajectory explorer. An earlier all-lanes default mixed the
two planes (operator-reported, 2026-08-13) and was reversed. Residual:
a coding agent deliberately routed through a /up/ lane (hermes →
OpenRouter) still synthesizes; disable this key or give that agent a
dedicated upstream id if that matters for your deployment.

Default() seeds it true so the loader's partial-merge keeps it true
for an existing [observability] section that only sets `enabled` (the
CacheTrack partial-merge rule); it has no effect while Enabled is
false.

leaves.doc:
StoreContent is the node-local Plane A content key (D8, D17, F07):
when true, captured prompt, response and tool bodies of a hosted app's
spans (and the matching eval-dataset snapshots and admission excerpts)
are kept raw in this node's own obs_* tables, after mandatory secret
scrubbing. When false only their content hashes are kept, and span
events and links keep only their metadata attributes (names, ids,
types, models, usage counters).

It governs storage ON THIS NODE ONLY: node-local data never leaves the
machine. Whether raw content is pushed to an org is a separate
decision that stays with the existing raw-content predicate
([org_client.share] full_content / admin_managed or the signed
enterprise grant); this key never widens it. It is also separate from
those Plane B developer-privacy keys, which no longer decide whether a
hosted app's own content is stored locally.

Default true (Default() seeds it, so an [observability] section that
only sets `enabled` keeps it on). No effect while Enabled is false.
leaves.help: Keep the prompts, responses and tool inputs of your apps' traces on this machine, with secrets removed. Off keeps only their fingerprints and the traces' timings, models and token counts.

leaves.doc:
Destination is where the SDKs send an app's data by default: local,
online or both. Empty (the default) means local when this machine is not
signed in for SDK data and both when it is (it holds an SDK key, from
`observer sdk sign-in`), or online when it is signed in but does not
receive app data itself (app observability off or not in this build).
Choosing online or both sends an app's
spans off this machine, so the dashboard asks for confirmation and an
agent's MCP request waits for your approval.
leaves.help: Where the SDKs send an app's data by default: local, online or both. Empty (the default) means local when this machine is not signed in for SDK data and both when it is (it holds an SDK key, from `observer sdk sign-in`), or online when it is signed in but does not receive app data itself (app observability off or not in this build). Choosing online or both sends an app's spans off this machine, so the dashboard asks for confirmation and an agent's MCP request waits for your approval.

leaves.doc:
GatewayURL overrides the organization gateway address the SDKs send
online data to (scheme, host and port, for example
https://gw.example.com:4318). Empty (the default) uses the address the
organization returned when this machine signed in.
leaves.help: Overrides the organization gateway address the SDKs send online data to (scheme, host and port, for example https://gw.example.com:4318). Empty (the default) uses the address the organization returned when this machine signed in.

leaves.doc: Enabled gates sink construction. false ⇒ emit.Nop().
leaves.help: Turns self-monitoring on. It also needs the gateway address and a credential; nothing is sent without them.

leaves.doc: Endpoint is the OTLP/HTTP gateway endpoint (host:port or full URL).
leaves.help: The gateway address the records go to, as host:port or a full URL.

leaves.doc: KeyID / Secret compose the ingest credential; Token (if set) wins.
leaves.help: The id half of the gateway credential, used with the secret. A token wins when both are set.
The secret half of the gateway credential. Set it in the config file; it is never shown here.
A gateway token to use instead of the id and secret. Set it in the config file; it is never shown here.

leaves.doc: Insecure permits plaintext http:// (default requires https://).
leaves.help: Allow a plain http:// gateway address. Off requires https://.

leaves.doc: ServiceName overrides the OTLP resource service.name.
leaves.help: The service name the records carry. Empty uses superbased-observer.

leaves.doc:
RoutingSampleN controls routing Decide emission: 0 = off, 1 = every
decide, N = 1-of-N sample (plan fork 1; default 32).
leaves.help: How many model-routing decisions are sent: 0 sends none, 1 sends every one, and N sends one in N. The default is 32.

leaves.doc:
Enabled gates the whole rail. Default FALSE (zero value AND partial-
merge). Even when true, the daemon submits only while a valid consent
receipt exists (design §9.1/§9.3) — enabling in config alone never
bypasses consent.
leaves.help: Gates the whole rail. Default FALSE (zero value AND partial- merge). Even when true, the daemon submits only while a valid consent receipt exists — enabling in config alone never bypasses consent.

leaves.doc:
Endpoint is the collector URL the coarsened monthly aggregate would be
POSTed to. Validated at load: HTTPS-only, no credentials/query, host on
the approved list unless AllowCustomEndpoint. A change invalidates the
consent receipt (re-consent required). Default DefaultAggregateEndpoint.
leaves.help: The collector URL the coarsened monthly aggregate would be POSTed to. Validated at load: HTTPS-only, no credentials/query, host on the approved list unless AllowCustomEndpoint. A change invalidates the consent receipt (re-consent required). Default DefaultAggregateEndpoint.

§9.2): only with it true may Endpoint point at a non-approved host.
Default false.
leaves.help: The explicit self-host / testing escape: only with it true may Endpoint point at a non-approved host. Default false.

leaves.doc:
Enabled is the master switch. false ⇒ loopback-only (today's
behaviour); a non-loopback bind fails closed (plan §4.6). Even when
true, no listener binds non-loopback until Phase 2 wires the exposure
mode — Phase 1 assembles the substrate without exposing anything.
leaves.help: The master switch. false ⇒ loopback-only (today's behaviour); a non-loopback bind fails closed. Even when true, no listener binds non-loopback until Phase 2 wires the exposure mode — Phase 1 assembles the substrate without exposing anything.

leaves.doc:
Mode selects the exposure transport: off | tailscale | lan. Never a
bare "0.0.0.0" (plan §5). Phase 1 accepts only "off".
leaves.help: Selects the exposure transport: off | tailscale | lan. Never a bare "0.0.0.0". Phase 1 accepts only "off".

leaves.doc:
BindAddr is the EXPLICIT IP:port to bind in lan mode (plan §5 — never
0.0.0.0, never an interface name). Empty in off/tailscale mode.
leaves.help: The EXPLICIT IP:port to bind in lan mode. Empty in off/tailscale mode.

leaves.doc:
TailscaleBackendAddr is the dedicated LOOPBACK IP:port the tailnet-serve
backend binds in tailscale mode (plan §4.4 Phase 2). It MUST be a
loopback address distinct from the owner-trusted direct dashboard
listener: `tailscale serve` terminates TLS remotely and forwards
plaintext here, so this listener requires auth for EVERY request (no
RemoteAddr bypass) and is the ONLY place forwarded-identity headers are
consumed. Empty in off/lan mode; `observer remote enable --tailscale`
pins a randomized free loopback port here.
leaves.help: The dedicated LOOPBACK IP:port the tailnet-serve backend binds in tailscale mode. It MUST be a loopback address distinct from the owner-trusted direct dashboard listener: `tailscale serve` terminates TLS remotely and forwards plaintext here, so this listener requires auth for EVERY request (no RemoteAddr bypass) and is the ONLY place forwarded-identity headers are consumed. Empty in off/lan mode; `observer remote enable --tailscale` pins a randomized free loopback port here.

leaves.doc:
TrustedHosts are extra Host-header allow-list entries for the
browserGuard Host check on a remote-exposed bind (plan §4.5). Never
"allow any Host".
leaves.help: Extra Host-header allow-list entries for the browserGuard Host check on a remote-exposed bind. Never "allow any Host".

leaves.doc:
RequireTLS mandates TLS for ALL remote access (plan §5 — no plain-HTTP
data path). Default true; not waivable for a data-bearing view.
leaves.help: Mandates TLS for ALL remote access. Default true; not waivable for a data-bearing view.

leaves.doc:
AllowTerminal gates the execute-tier remote terminal surface (Phase 4).
Default false — off even for an execute-capable user until enabled.
leaves.help: Gates the execute-tier remote terminal surface (Phase 4). Default false — off even for an execute-capable user until enabled.

leaves.doc:
AllowRemoteTerminalTakeover controls whether a successfully authenticated
remote writer may supersede an existing local/native or remote writer.
Default true for seamless handoff; false preserves the explicit-yield
posture. This changes only post-authorization lease policy: AllowTerminal,
device authentication, launch policy, and the capability/standing-secret
credential gate remain mandatory and upstream. Local-only; never
distributed or server-forced.
leaves.help: Controls whether a successfully authenticated remote writer may supersede an existing local/native or remote writer. Default true for seamless handoff; false preserves the explicit-yield posture. This changes only post-authorization lease policy: AllowTerminal, device authentication, launch policy, and the capability/standing-secret credential gate remain mandatory and upstream. Local-only; never distributed or server-forced.

leaves.doc:
AllowTerminalView is the independent READ opt-in for remote VIEWING of
attach/resume terminals (session-attach design §3.2, Phase 4). It is
STRICTLY WEAKER than AllowTerminal (write): an attach/resume PTY binds a
daemon-owned terminal to a REAL external transcript whose TUI can echo
secrets/customer data, so this controls whether a remote paired device
gets the snapshot row AND the websocket subscription for such sessions.
Default TRUE — mirroring the AllowRemoteTerminalTakeover default-true
precedent. View-by-default is acceptable because the remote surface is
ALREADY multi-lever gated: it opens nothing until the operator arms the
rail and a paired device authenticates over the tailnet, and the remote
WRITE/drive path is UNCHANGED by this default — driving still requires
AllowTerminal AND the full execute-tier writer-acquire conjunction
(device auth + per-terminal approval / standing secret + takeover). The
toggle still exists: setting allow_terminal_view = false restores the
deny-read posture. Seeded true in Default(); BurntSushi's field-level
decode leaves an absent key untouched, so a legacy [remote] block that
predates the key loads as true while an explicit false sticks (the same
partial-merge mechanism AllowRemoteTerminalTakeover relies on). Never
distributed; never server-forced.
leaves.help: The independent READ opt-in for remote VIEWING of attach/resume terminals. It is STRICTLY WEAKER than AllowTerminal (write): an attach/resume PTY binds a daemon-owned terminal to a REAL external transcript whose TUI can echo secrets/customer data, so this controls whether a remote paired device gets the snapshot row AND the websocket subscription for such sessions. Default TRUE — mirroring the AllowRemoteTerminalTakeover default-true precedent. View-by-default is acceptable because the remote surface is ALREADY multi-lever gated: it opens nothing until the operator arms the rail and a paired device authenticates over the tailnet, and the remote WRITE/drive path is UNCHANGED by this default — driving still requires AllowTerminal AND the full execute-tier writer-acquire conjunction (device auth + per-terminal approval / standing secret + takeover). The toggle still exists: setting allow_terminal_view = false restores the deny-read posture. Seeded true in Default(); BurntSushi's field-level decode leaves an absent key untouched, so a legacy [remote] block that predates the key loads as true while an explicit false sticks (the same partial-merge mechanism AllowRemoteTerminalTakeover relies on). Never distributed; never server-forced.

leaves.doc:
AllowStandingTerminalControl is the OPT-IN master switch for the standing
terminal-control secret (standing-terminal-access §B): a single durable,
hashed-at-rest secret that lets a paired device re-acquire writer control
across websocket refreshes WITHOUT a fresh per-terminal owner approval.
Default false. It is a STRICT SUPERSET of risk over the single-use flow —
anyone holding the secret + a paired session controls EVERY terminal — so
it lives beside allow_terminal (which it also requires) and is off until
the operator consciously mints a secret from the local dashboard. The raw
secret is never stored: its argon2id hash lives in a 0600 sibling file of
the pairing secret (remotecfg.StandingTerminalSecretPath).
leaves.help: The OPT-IN master switch for the standing terminal-control secret: a single durable, hashed-at-rest secret that lets a paired device re-acquire writer control across websocket refreshes WITHOUT a fresh per-terminal owner approval. Default false. It is a STRICT SUPERSET of risk over the single-use flow — anyone holding the secret + a paired session controls EVERY terminal — so it lives beside allow_terminal (which it also requires) and is off until the operator consciously mints a secret from the local dashboard. The raw secret is never stored: its argon2id hash lives in a 0600 sibling file of the pairing secret.

leaves.doc:
RevokeStandingOnTakeover is an OPT-IN hardening of standing access.
When true, a LOCAL (desktop) writer takeover of a remote writer that
held control through the standing credential also revokes that
credential itself (the same teardown as the dashboard explicit revoke
— verifier hot-disabled, remote writers dropped, credential file
removed). Default false — the seamless posture: takeover revokes only
the live lease and the paired device may re-acquire later. Local-only;
never distributed.
leaves.help: An OPT-IN hardening of standing access. When true, a LOCAL (desktop) writer takeover of a remote writer that held control through the standing credential also revokes that credential itself (the same teardown as the dashboard explicit revoke — verifier hot-disabled, remote writers dropped, credential file removed). Default false — the seamless posture: takeover revokes only the live lease and the paired device may re-acquire later. Local-only; never distributed.

leaves.doc:
WriterLeaseIdleMinutes is the idle lifetime of a remote writer lease
(Phase 4 §4.α.2c), refreshed on each Write/Resize. Default 5.
leaves.help: The idle lifetime of a remote writer lease, refreshed on each Write/Resize. Default 5.

leaves.doc:
WriterLeaseMaxMinutes is the hard cap on a remote writer lease's lifetime
(§4.α.2c) after which the holder must re-acquire. Default 30.
leaves.help: The hard cap on a remote writer lease's lifetime after which the holder must re-acquire. Default 30.

leaves.doc:
RateLimitPerMin caps auth attempts (code-server-class). Default 6.
0 disables limiting for the PAIRING endpoint only; the standing
terminal-control verifier clamps <=0 back to 6/min (each standing attempt
costs a 19 MiB argon2 compute, so it is never unlimited).
leaves.help: Caps auth attempts (code-server-class). Default 6. 0 disables limiting for the PAIRING endpoint only; the standing terminal-control verifier clamps <=0 back to 6/min (each standing attempt costs a 19 MiB argon2 compute, so it is never unlimited).

leaves.doc:
CapabilityTTLMinutes is the lifetime of a single-use terminal-control
execute capability + its bound confirm nonce (plan §4.2). Default 10.
Raised from a hard-coded 2 minutes on 2026-07-25: the codes are conveyed
out-of-band (email / chat / password manager) and the human round-trip
routinely outlasted a 2-minute window, so a code expired in transit and
had to be re-issued. This widens EXPOSURE TIME only — the capability stays
single-use, session+action+handle-bound, confirm-paired, and owner-loopback
minted. 0 uses the package default; set 2 to restore the old window.
leaves.help: The lifetime of a single-use terminal-control execute capability + its bound confirm nonce. Default 10. This widens EXPOSURE TIME only — the capability stays single-use, session+action+handle-bound, confirm-paired, and owner-loopback minted. 0 uses the package default; set 2 to restore the old window.

leaves.doc:
SessionTTLMinutes is the absolute device-session lifetime (plan §4.3).
Default 2880 (48 hours); a session older than this is rejected. Raised
from 720 (12h) on 2026-07-25 so the 24h idle target below is actually
reachable — an absolute cap under the idle bound makes the idle bound
unreachable. 48h (not the 7 days first implemented) is the operator's
chosen bound: one full idle window plus a day of headroom, at a fraction
of the exposure. 0 uses the package default (remoteauth.DefaultSessionTTL);
negatives are rejected at load.
leaves.help: The absolute device-session lifetime. Default 2880 (48 hours); a session older than this is rejected. Raised from 720 (12h) on 2026-07-25 so the 24h idle target below is actually reachable — an absolute cap under the idle bound makes the idle bound unreachable. 48h (not the 7 days first implemented) is the operator's chosen bound: one full idle window plus a day of headroom, at a fraction of the exposure. 0 uses the package default; negatives are rejected at load.

leaves.doc:
SessionIdleMinutes is the device-session idle timeout. Default 1440 (24h),
raised from 60 on 2026-07-25 at the operator's request: a paired phone put
down overnight must still be paired in the morning. A live attached
terminal viewer now also refreshes the clock, so this measures genuine
inactivity rather than time since the last page load. 0 uses the package
default (remoteauth.DefaultSessionIdle); negatives are rejected at load,
as is an idle window LONGER than SessionTTLMinutes (the absolute cap would
silently make it unreachable).
leaves.help: The device-session idle timeout. Default 1440 (24h), raised from 60 on 2026-07-25 at the operator's request: a paired phone put down overnight must still be paired in the morning. A live attached terminal viewer now also refreshes the clock, so this measures genuine inactivity rather than time since the last page load. 0 uses the package default; negatives are rejected at load, as is an idle window LONGER than SessionTTLMinutes (the absolute cap would silently make it unreachable).

leaves.doc: MaxSessions caps concurrent device sessions (plan §4.3). Default 5.
leaves.help: Caps concurrent device sessions. Default 5.

leaves.doc: Enabled gates the rail. Default false ⇒ no outbound call.
leaves.help: Gates the rail. Default false ⇒ no outbound call.

leaves.doc: Kind is the transport: webhook | ntfy. Default "webhook".
leaves.help: The transport: webhook | ntfy. Default "webhook".

leaves.doc: URL is the delivery endpoint (a webhook receiver or an ntfy topic URL).
leaves.help: The delivery endpoint (a webhook receiver or an ntfy topic URL).

leaves.doc:
Events subscribes to lifecycle events. Empty ⇒ all known events.
Default ["session_blocked", "session_finished"].
leaves.help: Subscribes to lifecycle events. Empty ⇒ all known events. Default ["session_blocked", "session_finished"].

leaves.doc:
BaseURL is the cloud service base URL, used only when neither
--base-url nor SBO_CLOUD_BASE_URL is set. Empty means "not
configured here" — the command falls through to its own "pass
--base-url or set SBO_CLOUD_BASE_URL" error. When set, it must parse
as an absolute http:// or https:// URL (see validateCloud).
leaves.help: The cloud service base URL, used only when neither --base-url nor SBO_CLOUD_BASE_URL is set. Empty means "not configured here" — the command falls through to its own "pass --base-url or set SBO_CLOUD_BASE_URL" error. When set, it must parse as an absolute http:// or https:// URL.

leaves.doc:
LoginPort is the loopback port `observer cloud login`'s WorkOS PKCE
callback listener binds, used only when SBO_CLOUD_LOGIN_PORT is
unset. 0 means "not configured here" — the command falls through to
its own built-in default (9797). Must be 0 or a valid TCP port
(1-65535) — see validateCloud.
leaves.help: The loopback port `observer cloud login`'s WorkOS PKCE callback listener binds, used only when SBO_CLOUD_LOGIN_PORT is unset. 0 means "not configured here" — the command falls through to its own built-in default (9797). Must be 0 or a valid TCP port (1-65535) — see validateCloud.

leaves.doc:
AutoSync opts INTO the background sync service (arc 2 R2a). When true
AND the `observer start` daemon is running, the daemon periodically
spawns `observer cloud sync` as a SUBPROCESS (never in-process — the
daemon links no cloud network package; see cmd/observer/cloudautosync.go
for the zero-egress justification). It stays consent-gated: the spawned
sync sends nothing without a live grant, exactly like a manual run.
Default false — the plane is manual-only until the operator opts in.
leaves.help: Opts INTO the background sync service (arc 2 R2a). When true AND the `observer start` daemon is running, the daemon periodically spawns `observer cloud sync` as a SUBPROCESS (never in-process — the daemon links no cloud network package; see cmd/observer/cloudautosync.go for the zero-egress justification). It stays consent-gated: the spawned sync sends nothing without a live grant, exactly like a manual run. Default false — the plane is manual-only until the operator opts in.

leaves.doc:
AutoSyncIntervalMinutes is how often the background sync service (R2a)
spawns `observer cloud sync`. 0 means "use the built-in default"
(CloudAutoSyncDefaultMinutes, 15). Read only when AutoSync is true;
must be 0 or >= cloudAutoSyncMinMinutes (5) — see validateCloud.
leaves.help: How often the background sync service (R2a) spawns `observer cloud sync`. 0 means "use the built-in default" (CloudAutoSyncDefaultMinutes, 15). Read only when AutoSync is true; must be 0 or >= cloudAutoSyncMinMinutes (5) — see validateCloud.

leaves.doc:
AutoEnrich opts INTO automatic per-session enrichment (arc 2 R8: the
"automatically enrich my new sessions" toggle, default OFF and prominent
on the consent/settings surface). SUPERSEDED as of the value-upgrade
plan's W3 (2026-09-15): background enrichment is now governed entirely
by internal/store/cloudpolicy.go's cloud_enrich_policy row (`observer
cloud enable --no-background` / the dashboard's "Run in the background"
switch), which the daemon's auto-enrich loop (cmd/observer/
cloudautoenrich.go) reads live on every tick. This key is still parsed
(an existing config.toml with `auto_enrich = true` must not fail to
load) but has NO behaviour — nothing reads it anymore. Kept only for
the TOML key's sake; `observer cloud status` says so explicitly.
leaves.help: Opts INTO automatic per-session enrichment. This key is still parsed (an existing config.toml with `auto_enrich = true` must not fail to load) but has NO behaviour — nothing reads it anymore. Kept only for the TOML key's sake; `observer cloud status` says so explicitly.

leaves.doc:
AutoEnrichIntervalMinutes is how often the background auto-enrich loop
(cmd/observer/cloudautoenrich.go) sweeps for quiet, personal-authority
sessions to enqueue. 0 means "use the built-in default"
(CloudAutoEnrichDefaultMinutes, 5); must be 0 or >=
CloudAutoEnrichMinMinutes (1) — see validateCloud. The loop itself is
inert unless the developer's cloud_enrich_policy row is on with
background enabled; this only tunes the cadence once it is.
leaves.help: How often the background auto-enrich loop (cmd/observer/cloudautoenrich.go) sweeps for quiet, personal-authority sessions to enqueue. 0 means "use the built-in default" (CloudAutoEnrichDefaultMinutes, 5); must be 0 or >= CloudAutoEnrichMinMinutes (1) — see validateCloud. The loop itself is inert unless the developer's cloud_enrich_policy row is on with background enabled; this only tunes the cadence once it is.

leaves.doc:
AutoEnrichQuietMinutes is how long a session's newest action must be in
the past before the background loop treats it as "ended" and a
candidate for auto-enrollment (sessions.ended_at is NULL for practically
every captured session, so "ended" is always inferred from quiet, never
read off a column). 0 means "use the built-in default"
(CloudAutoEnrichQuietDefaultMinutes, 10); must be 0 or >=
CloudAutoEnrichMinMinutes (1) — see validateCloud.
leaves.help: How long a session's newest action must be in the past before the background loop treats it as "ended" and a candidate for auto-enrollment (sessions.ended_at is NULL for practically every captured session, so "ended" is always inferred from quiet, never read off a column). 0 means "use the built-in default" (CloudAutoEnrichQuietDefaultMinutes, 10); must be 0 or >= CloudAutoEnrichMinMinutes (1) — see validateCloud.

leaves.doc:
WorkOSClientID is the PUBLIC WorkOS OAuth client id `observer cloud
login` builds the AuthKit PKCE authorize URL with (and the refresh
broker re-exchanges through). It is NOT a secret — the WorkOS API key
is server-side only and never read on the node. Resolution: the
WORKOS_CLIENT_ID environment variable first, then this key (same
env > [cloud] precedence as base_url / login_port), else the compiled
default (DefaultCloudWorkOSClientID) that Default() seeds here. An
operator can still opt out entirely by setting
`workos_client_id = ""` explicitly in config.toml — an explicit empty
value overrides the seeded default (ordinary TOML partial-merge
semantics: a key present in the file is always applied, even when its
value equals the zero value), landing back in the honest "set
[cloud].workos_client_id or WORKOS_CLIENT_ID" state instead of opening
a browser to nothing. Editable from the dashboard's Cloud account
card; read per `observer cloud` invocation, so no restart.

It is NOT a secret — the WorkOS API key is server-side only and never read on the node. Editable from the dashboard's Cloud account card; read per `observer cloud` invocation, so no restart.

leaves.doc:
Enabled gates the whole feed client. Default TRUE (operator decision
2026-09-20): the feed is live so a standalone node's prices track the
public source. A node that wants zero egress sets this false, which
makes the feed inert — no feed is fetched and no feed source badge
renders — leaving it drivable only by a manual `observer pricing sync`.
leaves.help: Gates the whole feed client. Default TRUE: the feed is live so a standalone node's prices track the public source. A node that wants zero egress sets this false, which makes the feed inert — no feed is fetched and no feed source badge renders — leaving it drivable only by a manual `observer pricing sync`.

leaves.doc:
Auto turns on the BACKGROUND poller (in addition to the manual sync).
Default TRUE (operator decision 2026-09-20): an Enabled node polls on
the PollIntervalHours cadence without further setup. Set false to keep
the feed enabled but fetch only on an explicit `observer pricing sync`.
leaves.help: Turns on the BACKGROUND poller (in addition to the manual sync). Default TRUE: an Enabled node polls on the PollIntervalHours cadence without further setup. Set false to keep the feed enabled but fetch only on an explicit `observer pricing sync`.

leaves.doc:
URL is the feed endpoint. Default DefaultPricingFeedURL (the public
edge); overridable for testing / a self-hosted mirror.
leaves.help: The feed endpoint. Default DefaultPricingFeedURL (the public edge); overridable for testing / a self-hosted mirror.

leaves.doc:
PollIntervalHours is the Auto poller cadence. Default 24 (D2: the feed
moves daily at most and a 304 is cheap). Ignored when Auto is false.
leaves.help: The Auto poller cadence. Default 24. Ignored when Auto is false.
